items.title: CVE-2026-59310: VMware vCenter Path Traversal (CVSS 9.8) Actively Exploited by China-Nexus APT to Deploy Backdoors & Ransomware
items.summary: A critical path traversal flaw in VMware vCenter (CVE-2026-59310, CVSS 9.8) is being actively exploited by a China-nexus APT group. Attackers gain unauthenticated remote code execution and are deploying persistent backdoors alongside Babuk-derived ransomware payloads across compromised virtualization infrastructure. CISA added it to the KEV catalog.
items.why: CVSS 9.8 with nation-state exploitation and public PoC — vCenter is the nerve center of virtualized enterprise environments. Compromise means full control of all hosted VMs. Patch or network-isolate management interfaces immediately; hunt for lateral movement and Babuk ransomware IOCs.

items.title: CVE-2026-65400: Apple macOS Screen Sharing Auth Bypass (CVSS 9.8) & CVE-2026-55040 SharePoint Auth Bypass (CVSS 9.1) Added to CISA KEV
items.summary: CISA added two new critical flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog: CVE-2026-65400, an Apple macOS Screen Sharing authentication bypass (CVSS 9.8) allowing unauthenticated remote access, and CVE-2026-55040, a Microsoft SharePoint authentication bypass (CVSS 9.1) enabling unauthorized access to sensitive document libraries. Both are confirmed exploited in the wild.
items.why: Two high-value enterprise attack surfaces — macOS endpoints and SharePoint — with auth-bypass flaws under active exploitation. Organizations using either platform face real risk of data exfiltration or initial access. Apply patches immediately; federal agencies face mandatory remediation deadlines.

items.title: Salt Typhoon Compromises Networks in 80+ Countries — China-Linked APT Embeds C2 Infrastructure Inside Google Sheets
items.summary: Salt Typhoon (China-linked APT) has achieved one of the most expansive espionage campaigns on record, compromising networks across 80+ countries. A related China-nexus campaign simultaneously breached 50+ telecoms and government agencies across 42 nations. The threat actor is tunneling command-and-control traffic through Google Sheets to blend into legitimate cloud service traffic, defeating traditional C2 detection.
items.why: Embedding C2 in Google Sheets defeats most network-based detection tools since traffic appears as benign SaaS usage. The scale — 80+ countries and critical infrastructure globally — is unprecedented. Defenders should implement cloud-app anomaly detection and scrutinize unusual Google API activity from endpoints.

items.title: APT-C-60 Refreshes Japan-Targeting Campaign: Proton Drive Lures, Weaponized RAR Archives, LNK Multi-Stage Payloads
items.summary: APT-C-60 has updated its operations against Japanese organizations with new TTPs designed to improve detection evasion. Spearphishing emails now contain Proton Drive links (a trusted cloud storage provider) that deliver weaponized RAR archives. When extracted, LNK files trigger a multi-stage execution chain leading to persistent remote access tool installation.
items.why: Using legitimate cloud storage (Proton Drive) for payload staging is a living-off-trusted-sites technique that bypasses URL reputation filtering and many email security gateways. Japanese enterprises and their supply chains should audit inbound links pointing to Proton Drive and enable LNK-file execution monitoring.

items.title: CyberStrikeAI: AI-Orchestrated Offensive Framework with 100+ Tools Detected on 21 Threat-Actor IPs Within 37 Days of Release
items.summary: CyberStrikeAI, a newly released AI-orchestrated offensive framework integrating 100+ tools with Model Context Protocol (MCP) support, was detected in active adversarial use on 21 IP addresses across China, Singapore, and Hong Kong within just 37 days of public release. The framework enables fully automated recon-to-exploitation pipelines with zero human intervention, representing a new class of AI-native offensive capability.
items.why: The 37-day threat-actor adoption timeline is alarming and signals the era of AI-accelerated offensive automation. CyberStrikeAI and its peers (70+ similar tools released in 18 months) are already in adversary hands. Defenders must assume AI-driven scanning and exploitation attempts are now routine and tune detection accordingly.
